## How It Works

Diagnose a broken web service by checking service health, logs, and network exposure; identify whether firewall or SELinux blocks access; apply persistent fixes and verify reboot stability.

## Key Points

- **Diagnosis scope**: inspect systemctl, journalctl, and socket state to locate the failure.
- **Remediation steps**: configure firewall for 8080, adjust SELinux port context, and enable service at boot.
- **Validation**: curl health endpoint and verify logs and boot persistence.

## Example

```bash
# Minimal working example
systemctl status httpd
journalctl -u httpd -xe
ss -ltnp | grep 8080
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8080/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
getenforce
sudo setenforce 0
sudo semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8080
sudo restorecon -Rv /var/www/html
sudo systemctl enable httpd
sudo systemctl restart httpd
curl -sSf http://localhost:8080/health || true
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical familiarity with user management, systemd services, sandboxing, and log rotation in RHCSA.

## Key Concepts
- systemd service units
- File permissions and ownership
- logrotate configuration
- PrivateTmp and ProtectSystem sandboxing

## Code Example
```bash
# status.sh
#!/bin/bash
uptime
whoami
```
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/demo-status.service
[Unit]
Description=Demo status service for user demo
[Service]
User=demo
Group=demo
ExecStart=/home/demo/status.sh
Restart=on-failure
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=full
StandardOutput=append:/var/log/demo_status.log
StandardError=inherit
```
```bash
# /etc/logrotate.d/demo-status
/var/log/demo_status.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  compress
  missingok
  notifempty
  create 0640 demo demo
}
```
